title: Every mental power was acquired by gradation

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Every mental power was acquired by gradation

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Each mental power and capacity must have been acquired gradually, so psychology will rest on this foundation, and light will be thrown on the origin of man and his history.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Psychology will be based on a new foundation, that of the necessary acquirement of each mental power and capacity by gradation.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIV, “Recapitulation and Conclusion”; section “Effects of its adoption on the study of Natural history”. Scope: mental powers of animals, including man

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch14-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Some cognitive traits admit comparative tests, but 'each mental power' is too broad and requires substantial interpretation. Current open data are sparse and biased toward a few taxa.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For prespecified cognitive capacities, map standardized behavioral and neural traits onto phylogenies and test whether complex states arise through ordered intermediate states rather than abrupt transitions. Repeated graded sequences support the claim for those capacities.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Ancestral cognition does not fossilize directly.

Mental powers are heterogeneous and difficult to compare across species.

Phylogenetic gradualism can be mimicked by coarse trait coding.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Gradual acquisition would be testable if comparable cognitive scores existed across a phylogeny, and they do not exist as a public dataset. Scattered experiments and endocranial volumes cover a few faculties in a few clades and leave 'each mental power' unmeasured. Until those scores are collected on a common scale, the analysis cannot confirm or refute the claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On a phylogenetic tree, score each mental capacity on a common ordinal scale across animals and humans and test whether every capacity appears by intermediate stages rather than in a single jump. The claim is confirmed if each capacity has precursor states in related organisms or in the archaeological and fossil record, and refuted by a capacity whose first appearance has no structural or behavioral intermediate.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Brain-size and archaeological records do not resolve particular faculties such as language or abstraction.

A missing intermediate can always be assigned to an untested or extinct species, which weakens refutation.

Mental capacities are not measured on one scale across taxa, so published experiments cannot be stacked into a single analysis.
